learning_objective: 🎯 Discover what rights are, where they come from, and the critical balance between the rights we demand and the responsibilities we hold!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Rights are justified claims that we make on society and the state. They are essential conditions that help individuals develop their true potential.
Earlier, thinkers believed in 'Natural Rights' given by God (life, liberty, property). Today, we focus on 'Human Rights'—rights you have simply because you are a human being.
A claim becomes a legal right only when it is recognized by the state (usually written in a Constitution). The state is responsible for enforcing and protecting these rights.
Political Rights (right to vote), Civil Rights (freedom of speech, right to fair trial), and Socio-Economic Rights (right to minimum wage, education, health).
Rights are not absolute. They come with obligations. My right to swing my fist ends where your nose begins. We must respect the rights of others and protect the environment.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Rights Balancer
fun_activity.instructions: You have the 'right to free speech'. Think of a scenario where exercising your right to speak freely directly conflicts with someone else's 'right to a peaceful life'. How would you balance them?

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between a mere 'claim' (I want this) and a 'right' (a claim recognized by society and backed by the state).
📌 Immanuel Kant's view on human dignity is foundational to the modern understanding of Human Rights.
📌 Always mention that rights imply duties/responsibilities. They are two sides of the same coin.
quick_recap: ⭐ The UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights attempts to define the basic rights of all people in the world.
⭐ The right to life and liberty are considered the most fundamental of all rights.
⭐ Socio-economic rights are gaining importance as people realize political rights mean little if a person is starving.
